The company is also scouting for third-party project-management mandates to earn management fees.

risks.note: War in West Asia and the closure of the Straits of Hormuz are creating employment and livelihood uncertainty for the 3-4 million Indians working in the Middle East, a customer pool the company implicitly relies on; India's reliance on over $100 billion in remittances from this region could tighten under economic contraction there.
risks.risk: Geopolitical instability in West Asia affecting NRI/Gulf-linked customer base

risks.note: Restrictions on Russian oil imports imposed by the USA have removed a concessional supply source, creating budget-management pressure on the union government, an indirect cost/demand headwind for the sector.
risks.risk: Macro/fuel-cost pressure from disrupted oil supply

risks.note: The free trade agreement between USA and India remains unresolved, adding to broader economic uncertainty that could affect property demand.

The Tamil Nadu Apartment Ownership Act remains unimplemented; two of the company's three large redevelopment projects are proceeding on a 100% consent basis instead of the Act's 2/3rd consent threshold, a structural dependency on unanimous consent that could slow or block projects.
risks.risk: Regulatory uncertainty on redevelopment consent framework

risks.note: It is unclear whether the new Chennai airport will be located near Sriperumbudur, which may have a dampening effect on demand for the company's projects and land there.

risks.note: The Expressway to Bangalore is proceeding at a slow pace, causing repeated revisions to completion schedules for Sriperumbudur properties that depend on improved connectivity.

The company is still evaluating whether to approach the capital market for further capital augmentation and has not made a final decision; in the interim it depends on private debt funds and bank/FI construction finance, an unresolved capital-structure dependency.
risks.risk: Dependence on capital-market/financing decision still unresolved

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- distribution: track record of pricing power on completed city projects — evidence: the company states it understood "its marketing positioning and pricing power from the way these projects [Infinys, Rathirupa, Hiranmayi, Homeleigh, Sahana, Sankalp and Bagya] were priced, sold and the feedback it received from its customers"
- resource: land bank at Sriperumbudur available for phased senior-living and plotted development — evidence: company states "lands are available with the company" for further Harmonia villa phases and cites 9.5 lakh sq.ft of remaining land at the site

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- War in West Asia and the closure of the Straits of Hormuz are creating employment and livelihood uncertainty for the 3-4 million Indians working in the Middle East, a customer pool the company implicitly relies on; India's reliance on over $100 billion in remittances from this region could tighten under economic contraction there.
- Restrictions on Russian oil imports imposed by the USA have removed a concessional supply source, creating budget-management pressure on the union government, an indirect cost/demand headwind for the sector.
- The free trade agreement between USA and India remains unresolved, adding to broader economic uncertainty that could affect property demand.
- The Tamil Nadu Apartment Ownership Act remains unimplemented; two of the company's three large redevelopment projects are proceeding on a 100% consent basis instead of the Act's 2/3rd consent threshold, a structural dependency on unanimous consent that could slow or block projects.
- It is unclear whether the new Chennai airport will be located near Sriperumbudur, which may have a dampening effect on demand for the company's projects and land there.
- The Expressway to Bangalore is proceeding at a slow pace, causing repeated revisions to completion schedules for Sriperumbudur properties that depend on improved connectivity.
- The company is still evaluating whether to approach the capital market for further capital augmentation and has not made a final decision; in the interim it depends on private debt funds and bank/FI construction finance, an unresolved capital-structure dependency.
- Offtake for the Harmonia Pavilion apartment format and Harmonia Duplex Villas has been relatively slow, requiring the company to place special marketing emphasis, indicating demand-execution risk on newer formats.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue focus on residential properties and plotted land development, where the company has found good traction.
- Pursue re-development of ageing city housing-society and Housing Board properties more vigorously, minimising capital commitment to construction cost and premium FSI payment rather than land acquisition.
- Scout for management of third-party projects to earn project management fees.
- Expand senior-living format (Harmonia villas/apartments) at Sriperumbudur as demand accelerates, using land already owned by the company.
- Consider monetising remaining Sriperumbudur high-rise land as …
